question: What was the original main goal of introducing Universal Precautions?

options.A: Ensuring accurate diagnosis of chronic illnesses
options.B: Speeding up the admission process for new patients
options.C: Protecting health workers from bloodborne pathogens
options.D: Lowering the overall cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Universal Precautions were originally created specifically to shield healthcare staff from infections transmitted through blood and specific body fluids. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: How do Standard Precautions differ from original Universal Precautions?

options.A: Standard Precautions remove the need for handwashing if gloves are worn
options.B: Standard Precautions apply to all body fluids and moist tissues, not just blood
options.C: Standard Precautions ignore non-intact skin and focus solely on respiratory droplets
options.D: Standard Precautions are only used when a patient has a confirmed laboratory diagnosis

explanation: While Universal Precautions focused mainly on blood, Standard Precautions broaden the safety net to include all body fluids, secretions, and non-intact skin for every patient. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is maintaining infection control standards especially challenging in under-resourced hospitals?

options.A: A lack of interest from senior medical consultants
options.B: Excessive amounts of personal protective equipment
options.C: Patients refusing to take prescribed medications
options.D: Unpredictable water supply and shortages of basic safety supplies

explanation: Frequent utility failures and lack of continuous basic commodities make standard cleaning and barrier methods much harder to sustain daily. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: A nurse in a busy rural clinic runs out of sterile gloves during an emergency wound dressing. What is the safest clinical action?

options.A: Obtain fresh supplies or use available clean alternatives according to protocol, avoiding unsafe shortcuts
options.B: Cancel the procedure and send the patient home without care
options.C: Perform the procedure barehanded to save time
options.D: Reuse a discarded pair of gloves after washing them with cold water

explanation: Shortages should never excuse compromising basic safety; nurses must secure proper supplies or follow approved institutional alternatives. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: When must a pair of disposable medical gloves be changed?

options.A: Only when they show visible tears
options.D: At the end of an eight-hour shift

explanation: Gloves must always be changed between patients to prevent carrying micro-organisms from one person to another. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why must a nurse wash their hands immediately after removing gloves?

options.A: Gloves can have tiny invisible defects and hands can become contaminated during removal
options.B: Soap helps preserve the natural oils in the skin of the hands
options.C: Hospital policy requires handwashing only before putting on gloves
options.D: It removes any lingering powder left inside the glove material

explanation: Microscopic leaks or accidental contamination during glove stripping means hands are rarely completely clean underneath. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for choosing soap and water over alcohol rub?

options.A: Soap and water dry out the skin much faster
options.B: Hands are visibly soiled or contaminated with spore-forming germs
options.C: Alcohol rubs are too expensive to use in general wards
options.D: Alcohol rubs take longer to apply than washing

explanation: Visible dirt and certain tough bacterial spores require the physical scrubbing action of soap, water, and friction to be removed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which action represents the correct use of alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: Applying the rub and wiping the hands dry quickly with a cloth towel
options.B: Applying the rub and rubbing hands together until the solution is completely dry
options.C: Rinsing the hands with clean water right after applying the rub
options.D: Applying the rub only when wearing sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Alcohol rubs need to air-dry completely on the skin to achieve their full germ-killing effect. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the safest way to handle a needle after giving an injection?

options.A: Recap the needle firmly using both hands at the bedside
options.B: Place the syringe on the patient's bedside tray for later disposal
options.C: Drop it immediately into a puncture-resistant sharps box without recapping
options.D: Bend the needle tip to prevent accidental sticking before disposal

explanation: Immediate disposal into a dedicated container without attempting to recap eliminates most accidental needle puncture risks. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: When should a safety sharps container be sealed and replaced?

options.A: Whenever a new nursing shift begins
options.B: Only when it is filled completely to the very top rim
options.C: At the end of every working week regardless of level
options.D: When it reaches the three-quarters full mark

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters full prevents protruding items from accidentally sticking staff who try to push more waste inside. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which type of waste belongs in the black-colored hospital bin?

options.A: Disposable syringes and metal scalpel blades
options.B: Non-hazardous domestic trash like office paper and food wrappers
options.C: Used surgical gauze soaked in patient blood

explanation: Black bins are designated for ordinary non-clinical waste that does not pose an infection or sharps hazard. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: A patient's surgical wound leaks blood onto the ward floor. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Leave the spill to dry before sweeping it up with a broom
options.B: Mop the area quickly with dry paper towels without wearing gloves
options.C: Put on appropriate gloves and apply a chlorine disinfectant solution over the spill
options.D: Call the administrative office to report a building maintenance issue

explanation: Protecting oneself with barriers and disinfecting the fluid immediately prevents the spread of bloodborne germs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after experiencing a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Fill out an official hospital incident report form
options.B: Wash the affected skin thoroughly with soap and running water
options.C: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out as much blood as possible
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to see if swelling develops

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral load introduced by the sharp object before it establishes infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is time critical when starting Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV after an exposure?

options.A: Hospital insurance only covers the drugs on the first day
options.B: Delayed treatment makes the medication toxic to the kidneys
options.C: PEP works best when started very soon after exposure, ideally within 72 hours
options.D: The virus disappears from the bloodstream after three days

explanation: Starting medications quickly stops the virus from replicating and establishing a permanent infection in the body. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is a major focus of infection control education during community health nursing outreach?

options.A: Encouraging residents to avoid visiting local healthcare clinics
options.B: Training villagers to perform complex surgical procedures at home
options.C: Teaching families practical hygiene habits and safe home care for sick relatives
options.D: Promoting the purchase of expensive hospital-grade air purifiers

explanation: Community nursing focuses on empowering families with simple, low-cost habits that prevent disease transmission at home. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: A community health nurse notices that traditional birth attendants in a local village reuse unsterilized razor blades. What is the most appropriate intervention?

options.A: Provide education on safe cutting practices and supply proper sterile instruments
options.B: Report the village to the police for practicing illegal medicine
options.C: Ignore the practice since it is part of local cultural heritage
options.D: Refuse to visit the village until the elders sign a formal apology

explanation: Respectful education paired with accessible tools helps change dangerous habits without alienating traditional birth attendants. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)
